title: Private upgrades: backup orchestrator + snapshot hooks (CSI/EBS) + optional logical backup
author: Irene Choi
release_notes: Adds installer-managed backups for Private upgrades: pre-upgrade snapshot hooks (CSI/EBS) and optional logical DB backups with progress reporting. Persists backup metadata into upgrade state for auditability and rollback workflows. Improves failure handling with clear remediation output and a safe abort path when backups fail.
description: Summary: This PR adds a first-class backup orchestration phase to the Private upgrade workflow. The installer now runs a pre-upgrade backup step that can (a) create volume snapshots via pluggable snapshotters (initial support: Kubernetes CSI VolumeSnapshot and AWS EBS snapshots via CSI annotations) and/or (b) perform an optional logical DB backup (pg_dump) when snapshots are unavailable or when operators request an additional safety net. The orchestrator emits structured progress events (for CLI + future UI) and persists backup metadata into the upgrade state store so rollback and support bundles can reference what happened. Motivation: We’ve had multiple upgrade incidents/near-misses where rollback was risky because there was no deterministic backup step or because snapshot behaviors differed across environments. This change makes upgrades safe-by-default and reduces operator guesswork, aligning with ENG-4838 and the broader “Private upgrade + rollback mechanism” project. Design/behavior: 1) New phase in plan execution: pre_upgrade_backup runs after prechecks and before any control-plane schema migrations or chart changes. 2) Backup strategies: SnapshotBackup (preferred) creates snapshots for PVCs selected by label/allowlist (db, control-plane state, queue/cache if configured). Uses CSI VolumeSnapshot API if supported; falls back to an AWS EBS snapshot flow when running on EKS with the EBS CSI driver (detected via StorageClass provisioner + PV topology). LogicalBackup (optional) runs a job in-cluster to produce a compressed pg_dump stored to a configured object store endpoint or a local path in on-prem mode. The logical backup is explicitly opt-in (--backup.logical.enabled) and requires credentials/target to be present. 3) Encryption and access: The orchestrator enforces encryption expectations when possible (e.g., checks StorageClass parameters / snapshot class annotations). For logical backup targets, it validates that the destination is configured for server-side encryption when supported (S3 SSE-S3/SSE-KMS) and warns otherwise (non-blocking). 4) Progress reporting: Standardized events are emitted for start/progress/complete/failure with stable step IDs. CLI prints a compact progress view; verbose mode includes per-volume timing and snapshot IDs. 5) Failure handling: Backup failures are blocking by default (upgrade aborts before any mutations). Partial snapshot creation is treated as failure; the output includes the created snapshot IDs to help cleanup. A --backup.continue-on-failure flag exists for break-glass situations (hidden; requires confirmation prompt). 6) Auditability: The upgrade state store now records backup artifacts (snapshot IDs, VolumeSnapshot names, logical backup URI, timestamps, duration, and validation status). This is used by future rollback commands and included in support bundles (ENG-4899 follow-up will wire the bundle). Operator UX: New installer flags: --backup.enabled (default true for upgrade), --backup.strategy=snapshot|logical|snapshot+logical, --backup.snapshot.pvcSelector (label selector), --backup.logical.enabled, --backup.logical.destination (s3://… or file:///…), --backup.timeout, --backup.continue-on-failure (hidden). New commands: redwood-private upgrade plan now includes a Backup stage when enabled; redwood-private upgrade run prints a Backup section with progress. Notably, this PR does not implement restore; restore/rollback hooks will consume the recorded artifacts (ENG-4844 / PR-4862). Testing: Adds unit tests for snapshot selection, CSI capability detection, and state persistence. Adds an integration test job in CI that runs a mocked snapshotter and verifies that upgrade plan execution halts on backup failure. Limitations: On-prem snapshot support depends on the cluster’s CSI driver exposing VolumeSnapshot. If VolumeSnapshot CRDs are missing, snapshot backups will fail with a clear remediation message (install snapshot-controller + CRDs) and operators can choose logical backups instead. Logical backup currently supports Postgres only (our control-plane DB). Follow-ups: (1) Add restore hooks + verification checks for snapshots and logical backups (ENG-4838). (2) Support additional snapshot backends and explicit SnapshotClass selection (requested by design partners). (3) Wire backup metadata into support bundle and audit log events (ENG-4899 + redwood monorepo PR for audit logging).

conversation_summary: Sean Gallagher: Can we make backup failure blocking by default? We should not mutate anything without a backup artifact recorded. Irene Choi: Yes—default is blocking; added explicit abort semantics and a hidden continue-on-failure flag with confirmation. Connor O'Brien: How does this behave for air-gapped/on-prem where S3 isn’t available? Irene Choi: Snapshot is the preferred path; logical backups can write to file:/// mounted paths. Added validation + remediation text if VolumeSnapshot CRDs are missing. Hanae Suzuki: Please confirm that state persistence doesn’t store credentials. Irene Choi: Backup destinations/credentials are read from existing secret refs; upgrade state stores only redacted URIs and snapshot IDs; added tests for redaction. Vanessa Ortiz: Snapshot selection needs to be explicit; we can’t snapshot everything by default. Irene Choi: Added allowlist labels + pvcSelector flag; default matches only control-plane DB + state PVC labels. Rafael Mendes: Add timeouts and surface duration in output so on-call can reason about stuck backups. Irene Choi: Added per-step timeout and duration metrics in progress events and state.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash after approvals; queued for inclusion in the next Private release train once ENG-4834 preflight framework lands in release branch.
